observation.visible_scene: Two upright mannequins with metallic foil faces, wide-brimmed hats and white lab coats stand side by side on a circular platform, framed by silver metal truss towers against a clear blue sky, dry desert hills and a white fabric barrier. A tall red-and-grey panel (with faint scale numbers) sits behind them. The scene is lit by hard daylight.
visible_changes: From t=0 to about t=1.0s the mannequins and platform are motionless; the view slowly enlarges (a gradual zoom/push-in), so the truss legs drift toward the frame edges and the red panel with numbers becomes more visible behind them.
At t~1.08s a bright yellow-orange flash appears at the right mannequin's shoulder/arm, and a white burst begins at the left mannequin's head/upper body.

From t~1.17s onward a dense white cloud erupts and expands radially outward, engulfing both figures; the lab coats visibly shred, and torn white fabric strips are thrown outward, most notably a long sleeve piece flying to the right.

The hats are pushed upward and remain perched atop the billowing cloud, then become partly obscured; the cloud keeps expanding and churning, filling most of the frame by the end while the mannequin bodies are largely hidden behind it.
The slow zoom continues through the burst, so the cloud occupies progressively more of the view.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the flash and white burst (impact, detonation or staged effect) is not shown.
What happens after the cloud dissipates (whether the mannequins are destroyed, melted or merely obscured) is beyond the excerpt.
The state of the scene before t=0 (any prior motion or setup) is not visible.
uncertain_details: The identity of the white material (smoke, powder, steam or shredded foam) cannot be confirmed.
Whether the apparent enlargement is an optical zoom or physical camera movement is not certain; background hills stay roughly fixed, suggesting little lateral camera motion.
It is unclear whether the left mannequin's head is destroyed or simply hidden by the cloud.
The relative left-right positions of the two figures stay the same throughout; observed change is expansion and fragmentation, not translation of the bodies.
